proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the original full-record endpoint minimax equality and matched precision/consistency frontier, then added bounded-loss transfer, unrestricted schedules, optimized-design equality, an erasure quotient and a finite squared-loss count program. Independent mathematics and citation checks passed, and graph fsck verified all 48 commits; no Lean formalization was started. The package remained incremental (score ceiling 5.6 below field threshold 7.4), so it was banked downgraded; the sparse-exposure Poisson minimax risk curve and sharper quantitative inference require a new research anchor.
tldr: For the atom-inclusive finite-population rollout-tail contrast on \(b\) disjoint bounded affine blocks with \(d\) fair independently assigned sources, the complete numerical record has exactly the endpoint-bit and explicit three-symbol erasure-game minimax value for every bounded Borel decision loss, with randomized actions retained. The same fixed-design value holds for all bounded block responses. Under squared loss, permutation reduction gives an exact convex two-count program with \((b+1)(b+2)/2\) action coordinates; at \(d=1\) it is the published \(\rho(b)\) game. The fixed-design risk has matched order \(\min\{1,2^d/b\}\), an explicit endpoint estimator, and uniform consistency exactly when \(b2^{-d}\to\infty\); the lower order already holds with strictly positive coefficients. Supported continuous affine concealment and explicit public-seed splitting prove the full numerical-record comparison. Over all parameter-independent source designs, both classes instead have the corresponding binary design-optimized value. For squared loss this is \(\rho(b)\), attained by independent fair coherent whole-block assignment and of order \(b^{-1}\). These are minimax-value identities, without pointwise sufficiency or Blackwell equivalence. The note provides a physical numerical-additivity benchmark for the reported RUMI simulation workflow, without imposing or contradicting its conditional-CDF-additivity condition.
gap: Published low-order numerical-response guarantees concern means. Generic exposure reductions zero irrelevant outcomes, which is not closed within the bounded affine class. Conditional-CDF additivity and regular quantile theory impose other structure.
fill: The supported affine concealment question and squared-loss transfer deliver \(R=R_E\) over the unrestricted bounded affine class; evaluated upper and lower bounds then locate its exact consistency boundary. A newly maintained strictly positive-coefficient subclass shows that the lower bound survives monotone physical response without restricting the headline class.
